guards.trigger: parent computed display is grid or inline-grid
guards.why: the item's containing block is its GRID AREA, which no probe measured; the proven /changelog defect (624px item emitted as 48.75% of the 1280px parent, resolved against the 624px area, rendered 303.27px)

guards.trigger: parent display flex/inline-flex AND flex-direction row|row-reverse AND (flex-grow > 0 OR flex-basis != auto)
guards.why: the used main-axis size comes from the flex base size grown/shrunk by free space, not from a fraction of the content box
guards.notRefused: flex-grow: 0 + flex-basis: auto in a row container, and every child of a column container (main axis is vertical)

guards.trigger: position:absolute and the parent does NOT establish a containing block (position static AND transform/filter/perspective none AND no will-change/contain hint)
guards.why: the containing block is some ancestor; the parent's box is unrelated to this node's width. Conservative by design: a property the Observer does not record reads as absent and therefore refuses

guards.trigger: position:absolute, the parent IS the containing block, but the parent has non-zero horizontal padding or border
guards.why: an absolutely positioned child resolves against the parent's PADDING box, which is exactly the quantity contentAt() subtracts away
guards.notRefused: position:absolute inside a zero-padding, zero-border positioned parent (the two boxes coincide)

guards.why: the containing block is the viewport (or a transformed ancestor) — never the parent's content box, at any width

guards.reason: (correction, not a guard) parent border subtracted from contentAt()
guards.why: the parent's content box is its border box minus padding AND border; the original code subtracted only padding, the fourth containing-block error 28.5A named. Chromium serializes computed `border-left` as `<width> <style> <color>`, so the leading length is parsed

it emits max-width + margin-inline:auto + width:auto — a cap and a centering, not a fraction of the parent — so the brief scopes guards to the two branches that DIVIDE by contentAt(). The browser truth check is its backstop and does reject it when it regresses.

truthCheck.mechanism: src/reconstruction/layout-truth-check.ts serializes the reconstruction's OWN emitted desktop RuntimeNode tree back into static HTML inside the same `.wr-variant[data-wr-viewport=desktop][data-wr-page=...]` wrapper PageRenderer.tsx produces, so the (0,3,0) recovered selectors match exactly as they will in the app. It loads that document in Chromium at the page's truth viewport with the app's real generated stylesheet (globals + exact computed classes + pseudo tier + observed-target tier) plus one empty `<style id="wr-layout-candidates">`, all remote schemes aborted at the route level so the render is offline and deterministic. It measures every candidate rule's `[data-wr-node]` rect with the candidate tier EMPTY — the baseline, i.e. what the exact computed fallback alone renders — then swaps only that style element's text and re-measures; there is no navigation and no re-parse, so each extra round costs one reflow. A candidate is REJECTED when max(|dx|,|dwidth|) against the observed truth rect exceeds TRUTH_SANITY_TOLERANCE_PX (4) AND exceeds the baseline error by more than 0.5px: the first half says the rule is wrong, the second says the RULE — not the reconstruction's own unavoidable drift from absent images and substituted fonts — is what made it wrong. Rejecting changes the layout, so survivors are re-measured up to MAX_ROUNDS (4) and then confirmed once more; if a page's set never settles, every remaining truth-checkable candidate on it is dropped whole (prefer rejection over clever math) and `truthCheckConverged` goes false. `responsive-hidden` rules are accepted unchecked and counted separately: their @media bands are built between a visible and a hidden probe width with the truth width always on the visible side, so they cannot apply at the truth viewport at all.
truthCheck.integratedAt: src/reconstruction/generate-app.ts:232 — inside generateApp(), before the generated stylesheet is written, so it is on the real `pnpm reconstruct` path (src/cli-reconstruct.ts:295 -> generateApp) and equally on the QA-correction path (src/reconstruction-qa/apply-corrections.ts:119) and the E2E path (src/e2e/run-reconstruction.ts:84). Only rules the re-render confirmed reach `generated-styles.css`.

failureModes.chromium-unavailable: playwright import or chromium.launch() failing is logged and recorded as manifest layout.truthCheckStatus = "chromium-unavailable". Rules pass through unfiltered — recovery failing must never fail the page — but the artifact says plainly that it was never verified.
failureModes.disabled: GenerateAppOptions.verifyLayout: false records "disabled". There is no path that skips the check and still claims verification.
failureModes.no-candidates: inference emitted nothing checkable; no browser is launched.

risks.risk: Generation determinism now depends on Chromium producing identical rects for identical content. smoke-reconstruction's byte-identical double-generation check passes today because its fixture has no layout probe (0 candidates, no browser). A corpus WITH candidates has not been double-generated.
risks.mitigation: the render is offline, fixed-viewport, deviceScaleFactor 1, with a fixed round budget; no clock or randomness enters the artifact (elapsedMs is returned to the caller but deliberately never written to the manifest). Worth one explicit double-generation on a probed corpus before release.

risks.risk: The differential (worse-than-baseline) acceptance rule is what prevents mass over-rejection when the reconstruction is already drifting for unrelated reasons (absent images, substituted fonts). If a future change made the harness render systematically differently from the real Next app, rules could be judged against the wrong baseline.
risks.mitigation: the harness serializes the SAME RuntimeNode IR the app renders and reuses the same wrapper attributes and the same generated CSS. The suite asserts the serializer's attribute mapping. A divergence would show as a large baseline error, not a silent acceptance.

risks.risk: Guards are conservative and will refuse some legitimately recoverable nodes (any grid item, any grown flex item). 28.5A's ablation says dropping the 52 percentage rules reproduces a full deletion's /changelog gain to 4 dp and is the best off-viewport state at 1920, so this is the measured-correct direction — but recovered-rule counts on a real corpus will fall.
risks.mitigation: refusal is free by design (the node keeps its exact computed style) and every refusal is counted by reason in the manifest, so the cost is visible rather than silent.

risks.risk: acceptedRegressed is measured only at the TRUTH viewport. Nothing here says anything about 1920 or 390; off-viewport behaviour remains inference, exactly as the `layout-rule-inferred` limitation already states.
risks.mitigation: none needed — the scope is stated. Change 3 was scoped to truth-viewport safety.

risks.risk: The truth check adds a chromium launch to every generateApp() call that has candidate rules, including inside other suites (smoke-e2e, smoke-reconstruction-qa) and inside src/production and src/release paths that regenerate.
risks.mitigation: zero-candidate plans launch nothing; `verifyLayout: false` is available and is recorded as "disabled" rather than silently passing. Measured cost is sub-second.

risks.risk: position:absolute guard reads `will-change`, `contain` and `perspective`, which are NOT in the Observer's STYLE_WHITELIST. They read as absent.
risks.mitigation: absent reads as 'does not establish a containing block', which REFUSES. The failure direction is safe by construction; it can only over-refuse, never under-refuse.
